member.summary: When set to true, enables the /refresh endpoint that allows clients to refresh their authentication token without disconnecting. The server will re-authenticate the request and update the connection's .

member.name: P:Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.Connections.HttpConnectionDispatcherOptions.OnAuthenticationRefresh
member.summary: An optional callback invoked when the /refresh endpoint has successfully re-authenticated the request but before the connection's user is replaced. Return true to accept the new principal, or false to reject the refresh. When rejected, the endpoint responds with HTTP 403 and the connection's current user remains in place.
member.remarks:
This callback is an additional policy applied on top of the connection's default identity association check (or an application-provided
override): both must accept the refresh for it to be applied. It cannot be used to bypass that underlying identity check.

member.name: P:Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.Connections.HttpConnectionDispatcherOptions.MaximumAuthenticationExpiration
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum amount of time, relative to now, that a refreshed authentication expiration is allowed to advance to, regardless of the expiration reported by the authentication ticket. Set to to leave the ticket's own expiration (or lack of one) unmodified. When set, the value must be greater than .
member.remarks: This applies whenever is true, including when the authentication ticket does not itself set an expiration. It does not affect the safety behavior for Windows authentication, whose expiration is never tracked or refreshed by this feature.

member.summary: Creates the DefaultConnectionContext without Pipes to avoid upfront allocations. The caller is expected to set the and pipes manually.
Updates the User/ClaimsPrincipal on this connection and refreshes the authentication expiration.
member.param: The refreshed principal to apply to the connection.
The expiration of the refreshed authentication.
The request context exposed to while validating the refreshed principal.
An optional additional policy invoked after accepts the refresh.
The request context to associate with the connection when publishing the refreshed principal.
member.remarks: This uses a two-phase validate-then-publish strategy: is awaited without holding (it may run arbitrary, possibly slow, application code), and the staleness/identity checks are then re-validated atomically with the swap under the lock. This prevents a concurrent refresh (for example the /refresh endpoint racing a long-polling poll) that already published a newer or different identity while the callback was running from being rolled back by this update. The update is skipped as if is older than the currently applied , or if the connection's user advanced past the snapshot this update's acceptance decision was based on.

member.name: T:Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.Connections.Internal.UserIdentitySnapshot
member.summary: An immutable snapshot of a principal's identity, used to decide whether a later request belongs to the same user as the one that negotiated a connection.

remarks.para: The snapshot is captured eagerly from a live . This matters because a subclass may decide for itself - is authenticated whenever it has a name, even though its is empty. Rebuilding such an identity as a base would silently make it unauthenticated and discard its identity claims.

Extraction follows the precedence used by antiforgery's DefaultClaimUidExtractor: the first authenticated identity carrying sub, , or wins. When no identity carries one of those, every authenticated claim is used instead, ordered so that claim ordering does not affect the result. When there are no authenticated claims, extraction follows DefaultAntiforgeryTokenGenerator and falls back to the first authenticated identity's nonempty .
